name: Inverse Multiquadric Splatting
definition: A splatting technique using an inverse multiquadric function as the radial basis function, requiring a correction factor to scale the 3D covariance matrix.
summary: Inverse Multiquadric Splatting is a radiance-field optimization technique that replaces standard Gaussian radial basis functions with inverse multiquadric functions to achieve slower-decaying splat tails.
